subsystems.name: Neural processing unit
subsystems.role: the accelerator that does the bulk of the arithmetic.

subsystems.name: Memory subsystem
subsystems.role: feeds weights and activations fast enough without draining the battery.

subsystems.name: Model representation
subsystems.role: a compressed form of the network small enough to fit and fast enough to stream.

subsystems.name: Runtime and compiler
subsystems.role: turns a trained model into a schedule of hardware kernels.
parts: dispatcher across NPU, GPU and CPU

subsystems.name: System integration
subsystems.role: connects the accelerator to the operating system and manages power and privacy.

buildSteps.title: Design the arithmetic units
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose which precisions to support in silicon — typically INT8 and INT4, sometimes FP16 — and lay out the multiply-accumulate arrays that dominate die area.

buildSteps.title: Write and verify the logic
buildSteps.detail: The design is expressed in a hardware description language, simulated, and formally checked, because a silicon error cannot be patched after fabrication.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and integrate the system-on-chip
buildSteps.detail: The accelerator is built on a leading-edge process node and wired into the chip alongside CPU cores, GPU, cache and LPDDR memory controllers.

buildSteps.title: Build the kernel and compiler stack
buildSteps.detail: Each supported operation gets a hand-tuned kernel; a compiler then fuses operations, tiles the work to fit on-chip memory, and schedules it.

buildSteps.title: Quantize a trained model
buildSteps.detail: Weights and activations are reduced from 16-bit floats to 8- or 4-bit integers using a small calibration dataset, or by retraining with quantization simulated in the loop.

buildSteps.title: Package and convert
buildSteps.detail: The quantized graph is converted into the runtime's format and partitioned: layers the accelerator supports stay on it, unsupported layers fall back to GPU or CPU.

buildSteps.title: Tune for power and heat
buildSteps.detail: Developers sweep clock speeds, batch sizes and memory traffic against a thermal budget, since a phone or laptop cannot dissipate what a data-centre card can.

buildSteps.title: Ship and update over the air
buildSteps.detail: Model files and drivers are delivered as updates, so a device learns new capabilities without new hardware.

prerequisites.why: 4-bit and 8-bit formats cut memory traffic by an order of magnitude, which is what makes local inference feasible.
dense multiply-accumulate arrays deliver the operations per watt that battery-powered devices need.
large models are memory-bandwidth-bound, so the win comes from moving bytes cheaply, not from raw compute.
running one model across many different accelerators still needs per-vendor tuning, so portability is improving but incomplete.
useful quality at a few billion parameters is recent; smaller models still trail large cloud ones on hard tasks.

pathway.milestone: flagship phones and laptops running several-billion-parameter models locally at tens of tokens per second
pathway.unlocks: offline assistants, live transcription and translation, and inference that never leaves the device.

pathway.milestone: sub-4-bit weights, mixture-of-experts routing and speculative decoding on-device
pathway.unlocks: larger effective models within the same memory and power envelope.

pathway.milestone: local personalization — on-device fine-tuning and retrieval over a user's own data
pathway.unlocks: assistants that adapt privately without uploading documents.

pathway.milestone: agentic workflows split between device and cloud, with the device deciding what may leave
pathway.unlocks: always-available automation where sensitive work stays local and heavy reasoning is offloaded.
